title: Precedence ordering
description: Policies carry precedence ranks, and higher-ranked policies win conflicts deterministically. Ranks reflect authority: legal holds outrank team preferences. The effective policy is computed by applying rules in rank order, so outcomes are predictable and explainable. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers precedence ranks per policy.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: [("team", 1, "allow"), ("legal", 5, "deny")], 2: [("team", 1, "deny"), ("legal", 5, "deny")], 3: [("team", 1, "allow")]}
rules = sorted(CFG[LEVEL], key=lambda r: -r[1])
winner = rules[0]
print("rules by rank:", rules, "| effective:", winner[2], "(from", winner[0], ")")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Overlap analysis
description: Policies covering the same resources are grouped so reviewers see the full rule set applying to any resource. Overlap is computed from scope expressions, not just names. Unexpected overlap is often where conflicts hide. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers grouping policies by covered resources.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: [{"db1"}, {"db2"}], 2: [{"db1", "db2"}, {"db2", "db3"}], 3: [{"db1"}, {"db1"}]}
scopes = CFG[LEVEL]
overlap = set.intersection(*scopes) if len(scopes) > 1 else set()
print("scopes:", scopes, "| overlapping resources:", sorted(overlap) or ["none"])
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Temporal conflict detection
description: Retention schedules and deletion deadlines are compared on the time axis: a 7-year retention rule conflicts with a 30-day deletion rule on the same data. Temporal conflicts are the most common cross-domain policy clash. Detection models each rule as a time interval and finds overlaps with opposing effects. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers modeling rules as time intervals.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: [("retain", 0, 2555), ("retain", 0, 2555)], 2: [("retain", 0, 2555), ("delete", 30, 30)], 3: [("delete", 30, 30), ("delete", 60, 60)]}
rules = CFG[LEVEL]
conflict = any(a[0] != b[0] and a[1] <= b[2] and b[1] <= a[2] for a in rules for b in rules if a is not b)
print("rules:", rules, "| temporal conflict:", conflict)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Conflict impact report
description: Each detected conflict gets an impact report: which resources, identities, and operations are affected, and what happens under each resolution. Impact turns abstract contradictions into concrete stakes for the resolver. Reports prioritize conflicts by blast radius. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers affected resources, identities, operations.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"resources": 2, "users": 10}, 2: {"resources": 15, "users": 200}, 3: {"resources": 100, "users": 5000}}
imp = CFG[LEVEL]
blast = imp["resources"] * imp["users"]
print("impact:", imp, "| blast radius:", blast, "| priority:", "P1" if blast > 10000 else "P2")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
